title: Assembled temp_por_top brown-out behavior across dip depth, hold duration, falling slew and recovery slew over the PVT grid
claim: Issue #116 (child of #106) -- NOT a spec claim: no ratified numeric brown-out envelope exists (DR-003 Sec8; spec/porting-plan.md Sec3.4 defines only the SHAPE of the three-axis sweep). Records, for the unchanged assembled design/temp_por_top.sch as committed in design/netlist/temp_por_top.spice (bias_core + temp_core + por_comparator + por_output_chain, real shared IBIAS node, real RESETn -> temp_core.EN feedback, no ideal bias or sensor substitution, PTAT/CTAT open), what RESETn does across an exploratory set of single supply dips (floor x hold x falling slew, plus recovery-slew variants and a no-dip control) x {tt,ss,ff,sf,fs} x {-40,27,125 C} x {2.97,3.30,3.63 V} starting supplies, graded from full-resolution RESETn/POR_RAW/VDD/IBIAS waveforms and the explicit delivered bias branch current (sim/brownout-top/brownout_checker.py). A completed simulation is not a behavioural PASS. gf180mcu numbers are not used anywhere; failed cells are evidence.
provenance_source: sim/brownout-top/testbench/tb_temp_por_brownout.sch (DUT: design/netlist/temp_por_top.spice, the committed export of design/temp_por_top.sch)
statistical_convention: N/A (corner-matrix check, not a distribution claim)

corners.supply_v_meaning: STARTING supply (VSET); the dip floor is absolute, so the excursion vf - vlow grows with the starting supply and every edge duration is derived from it

dut_loading.PTAT: open (no output buffer exists in the design)
dut_loading.RESETn: unloaded (no external load); drives only temp_core.EN internally
dut_loading.substitutions: none -- no ideal bias, no ideal sensor, no retired diagnostic XMN1 edit (the committed XMN1 is L=20 W=0.42 since #101/#111)

stimulus.construction: V(VDD) = min(vf, rup*t) - ex*( clip01((t-t0)*sf/ex) - clip01((t-t0-ex/sf-th)*sr/ex) ), ex = max(vf - vlow, 0).  Four independent axes: floor vlow, falling slew sf, hold th, recovery slew sr (+ t0).  The fall lasts ex/sf and the recovery ex/sr: durations are DERIVED from voltage excursion / slew, never a fixed duration, so the swept starting supply does not couple into either slew.  Implemented in the testbench BVDD source (SPICE twin of brownout_checker.vdd_expected, which the checker uses to verify the sampled VDD).
stimulus.power_up_note: 100 kV/s power-up (33 us ramp), one of the supply-ramp-top primary rates; chosen to keep the baseline short and cheap, not a claim about power-up behavior
stimulus.t0_rationale: dip starts 10 ms after power-up begins.  The supply-ramp-top as-drawn record 20261010-015905-fbd6329 shows RESETn releases (where they happen) between 1.5 and 4.3 ms at 100 kV/s and 1.8-4.3 ms at 10 kV/s over the whole PVT grid, so 10 ms is >2.3x the slowest observed release.  The checker additionally REQUIRES a viable baseline (exactly one release, RESETn settled high and delivered bias settled over the last 2 ms before t0) or the point is UNRESOLVED.
stimulus.observation_rationale: 10 ms after the recovery edge ends (tstop = t0 + fall + hold + recovery + 10 ms, taken at the largest starting supply): >2.3x the slowest observed release delay (4.3 ms).  A shorter record is truncated -> UNRESOLVED unless a failure is already detected.
stimulus.no_dip_control: vlow = 99 V (>= every starting supply, ex = 0): same power-up, baseline and window with no dip.  Any RESETn assertion is FAIL spurious_assertion_control; it also validates the baseline/observation windows per corner.
stimulus.tmax_rule: tmax = min(10 us, hold/6, shortest derived edge at the smallest starting supply / 12); recorded in each request.  The checker separately enforces a sample-gap limit (min(20 us, hold/5, shortest edge/10)) in the dip window, so tmax is inside it.
stimulus.cost_note: A first fleet attempt (run fleet1, 40 ms windows, tmax down to 0.5-1 us, 30 requests) hit the 3600 s batch timeout with ZERO usable corners on the first two requests (jobs klt-sim-63cf5157178b and klt-sim-415f0ec31ec1, runner concurrency 1): the grid was too expensive.  Windows, power-up rate, slew levels and tmax were reduced before the real submission; see the fleet1 timeout record.

grid.status: EXPLORATORY initial grid -- chosen to bracket, not to bound; NOT a specification envelope and NOT derived from any gf180mcu figure.
grid.rationale: Floors: 2.0 V is a shallow brown-out above half supply (never 'required-to-assert' under the declared detectability rule), 1.2 V is below half supply, 0.4 V is below V_IL at every starting supply (rail collapse).  Holds span 10 us - 1 ms (two decades).  Falling slews 2 kV/s and 50 kV/s (a ~2 V excursion in ~1 ms and ~40 us) -- two levels a factor 25 apart, kept few because simulation cost scales with 1/tmax and the first 3-level grid timed out on the fleet.  Faster slews (100 kV/s ... 1 MV/s need tmax <= 50 ns) are the first declared expansion (policy b).  Recovery slew is held at 10 kV/s for the full floor x hold x fall cube and varied one-at-a-time (1 kV/s, 100 kV/s) around the center point only -- a declared one-factor-at-a-time treatment of the fourth axis, not a full 4-D cube.
grid.request_count: 18 cube + 2 recovery variants + 1 no-dip control = 21 requests x 45 PVT points = 945 declared points
grid.expansion_policy: No envelope is claimed.  Expansion is a NEW record, never an edit: (a) if a boundary (PASS<->FAIL) appears between adjacent grid levels on any axis, add the midpoint level on that axis only at the affected corners; (a') a middle falling slew (e.g. 10 kV/s) and the 100 kV/s class are added next; (b) falling or recovery slews above 100 kV/s (first: 1 MV/s) need tmax <= 50 ns and a per-request cost estimate (the fleet1 timeout shows cost is binding) before they are added; (c) holds above 1 ms or below 10 us and floors between the three levels are added only with a stated reason; (d) the passive-skew (ll/hh) and mismatch axes are not in this increment.  Any post-hoc addition is labelled as such in its record, as in the #142 diagnosis.
grid.not_covered: dips below 0.4 V, above 2.0 V floor, holds outside 10 us - 1 ms, fall slews other than 2 kV/s and 50 kV/s and recovery slews outside 1 kV/s - 100 kV/s, dips starting from an unreleased state, repeated dips, ll/hh passive skew, mismatch Monte Carlo, PTAT/CTAT loading, post-layout parasitics.

grading.status: EXPLORATORY -- every number below is a measurement definition chosen for this campaign; none is a ratified bound, and none is a gf180mcu figure.
grading.levels: V_IL = 0.2 vf, V_IH = 0.8 vf, V_MID = 0.5 vf, V_MUST = 0.5 vf (vf = the point's starting supply)
grading.assertion: RESETn falls through V_IL starting from HIGH at t0 (Schmitt).  assertion_rail_limited is recorded when VDD itself was <= V_IL at that instant (the output could not stay high regardless of the comparator).  Release = RESETn rises through V_IH.
grading.detectability: a dip is 'required-to-assert' when VDD spends >= 50 us below V_MUST (piecewise-linear dwell from the full-resolution VDD).  Dips that are not required may assert or not -- both are recorded, neither fails -- but an assertion must still recover.
grading.baseline: viable when, before t0: exactly one RESETn release and no re-assert, RESETn >= V_IH over the 2 ms before t0, delivered bias branch current > 0 with peak-to-peak <= 5 % of its mean over that window.  Otherwise UNRESOLVED (the dip response cannot be attributed to the dip); detected codes are kept in 'detected_codes_ungraded'.
grading.failure_codes: missed_assertion; no_recovery; premature_release; reassert_after_recovery; reassert_chatter; not_high_at_end; bias_not_recovered; spurious_assertion_control (definitions in brownout_checker.py docstring).
grading.recovery: VDD recovered when >= 0.98 vf after the recovery edge starts; an assertion beginning later is reassert_after_recovery; two or more assertions are reassert_chatter; RESETn must be >= V_IH over the last 1 ms.
grading.delivered_bias: explicit measurement: drain current [id] of bias_core XMPIB (PMOS whose drain IS the IBIAS node), saved by the testbench as .save @m.xdut.xbias.xmpib.msky130_fd_pr__pfet_g5v0d10v5[id] and appearing in the klt waveform as i(@m.xdut.xbias.xmpib.msky130_fd_pr__pfet_g5v0d10v5[id]).  Sign: ngspice BSIM4 reports id POSITIVE for normal conduction in both polarities (verified by a local single-corner probe: XMPIB id ~0.78 uA equals the sum of the comparator, output-chain and temp_core diode devices' ids ~0.39+0.39+0 uA at 1.5 ms), so the delivered branch current is +id and must be positive at baseline (else NONPHYSICAL).  The consumer-side diode devices (comparator, output chain, temp_core XMBD [id]) are saved; their sum over the delivered current at the end is recorded (sink_sum_over_delivered_end).  The IBIAS NODE voltage v(xdut.ibias) is recorded separately and never used as a current.  End/baseline ratio band [0.8, 1.25] else FAIL bias_not_recovered.
grading.resolution: max sample gap from t0-10 us to VDD-recovery+100 us must be <= min(20 us, hold/5, shortest derived edge/10), AND sampled VDD must match the declared stimulus within 20 mV; otherwise a point with no detected failure is UNRESOLVED, not PASS.
grading.physicality: every saved node within [-0.3 V, vf+0.5 V] for t>0, settled supply current -i(BVDD) > 0, delivered bias positive at baseline.  Violation -> NONPHYSICAL (cannot PASS; behavioural verdict not graded).
grading.verdicts: ERROR (missing waveform / channel / non-finite data / convergence, model or backend error) > NONPHYSICAL > UNRESOLVED (unviable baseline, truncated, sparse, stimulus mismatch) > FAIL (resolved physical failure, with trace evidence) > PASS.  NOT_COVERED marks points whose request was never submitted, was refused by the fleet, or has no report; they are counted as uncovered, never as PASS.
grading.trace_storage: committed traces are change-triggered (dV >= 2 mV on any of VDD/RESETn/POR_RAW/IBIAS node, delivered bias moved >= 2 % of its maximum, or a 1 ms anchor); RESETn assertion/release counts are re-derived from the stored trace and compared with the full-resolution result per point.

default.label: default deck -- identical to the one submitted for record 20261010-222529-41bde9f

reltol2e-4.label: tightened relative tolerance (issue #153 companion re-grade of the NONPHYSICAL points)
reltol2e-4.rationale: #150 showed the two re-asserting supply-ramp points come back physical and resolved at reltol=2e-4 (optionally with tmax=1u), and #152 showed the temp_core cold-start FAILs do not reproduce on any solver variant: the NONPHYSICAL brown-out signature (temp_core-side nodes at impossible voltages, reversed settled supply current) is a solver-branch landing expected to move with integration tolerance.  tmax and every stimulus/window/checker setting stay at the declared default; this is a deck/solver variant, not a circuit change.
reltol2e-4.netlist_application: the extra options are appended to the testbench's single declared '.options method=gear trtol=50' line in the generated deck; circuit, stimulus parameters, .save channels, tstop/tmax, corner matrix and options.timeout_s=7200 are byte-identical to the default deck otherwise
reltol2e-4.status_note: Piloted on the batch fleet 2026-10-11 (record 20261011-214916-183a3fc): on the fleet's SPARSE solver it is x8-x20 slower and both pilot jobs hit the runner-enforced 3600 s whole-job limit; superseded as the active rerun variant by reltol2e-4-klu (see tightened_rerun.variant_decision). The variant stays declared; its pilot record stays as evidence.

reltol2e-4-klu.label: tightened relative tolerance + netlist-carried KLU direct linear solver (issue #153 companion re-grade of the NONPHYSICAL points)
reltol2e-4-klu.rationale: Declared 2026-10-12, before any submission under this variant (tightened_rerun.variant_decision).  Same reltol=2e-4 that #150 showed resolves the nonphysical branch, plus `klu`: the fleet runner ignores options.ngspice_init, so every fleet run so far executed ngspice's SPARSE default solver even though sim/spiceinit selects KLU for every local run of this repo, and carrying `klu` on the declared .options line is the only netlist-level way to select it there.  ngspice announces 'Using KLU as Direct Linear Solver' on stdout, which the retrieved per-point logs carry (per-point field netlist_klu_announced) as proof the fleet engaged it.  Changing the linear solver changes the rounding path, so the variant is declared and reported as tolerance + solver together, never as reltol alone.  tmax and every stimulus/window/checker setting stay at the declared default; this is a deck/solver variant, not a circuit change.
reltol2e-4-klu.netlist_application: the extra options are appended to the testbench's single declared '.options method=gear trtol=50' line in the generated deck; circuit, stimulus parameters, .save channels, tstop/tmax, corner matrix and options.timeout_s=7200 are byte-identical to the default deck otherwise

tightened_rerun.status: DECLARED before the run (issue #153); this section was committed before any tightened request was submitted.  Re-declared 2026-10-12 (variant_decision), still before any submission under the active variant: active variant reltol2e-4-klu and the observed 3600 s enforced job limit.
tightened_rerun.variant_decision: Declared 2026-10-12, before any submission under reltol2e-4-klu.  The first declared variant reltol2e-4 was piloted on the batch fleet (record 20261011-214916-183a3fc): both pilot jobs hit the runner-enforced whole-job limit -- the runner executes the job under `timeout 3600s` and ignores the request's declared options.timeout_s=7200 (2AMLogic/klayout-tools#2833 family; tracked for the runner as klayout-tools timeout handling) -- and klt discarded every corner, so all 90 pilot points are ERROR and no tightened point has been graded.  Measured cost of the tightened deck on SPARSE: whole-job ratio >= x8 (a lower bound: both pilots timed out) and x20 per corner on the slowest corner (ff/125C/2.97V control, local fleet-equivalent probe: 19 s default -> 389 s tightened).  Options considered, all pre-declared here: (a) one corner per job -- 45x the jobs against a shared fleet already refusing at BATCH_MAX_CONCURRENT_INSTANCES, plus per-corner request plumbing; rejected; (b) a longer job limit -- NOT AVAILABLE to this repo: the runner ignores the request's timeout_s, so raising it is a runner-side (2AMLogic/klayout-tools) change, not a manifest number; (c) a looser tolerance -- rejected: reltol=2e-4 is the value #150 showed resolves the nonphysical branch, and a tightened SPARSE probe still landed on the reversed-current branch at one source-physical control point, so loosening tolerance is more likely to land nonphysical, not less; (d) netlist-carried KLU -- CHOSEN as variant reltol2e-4-klu: it keeps the #150-derived reltol=2e-4, keeps whole-request granularity inside the enforced 3600 s limit (re-piloted and re-projected before the remaining requests are submitted, per cost_rule), and restores the solver every local run of this repo already uses via sim/spiceinit.  The choice was made on timing and transport evidence only -- no tightened point had been graded -- so nothing was selected from graded results.
tightened_rerun.rerun_set: every declared request.  All 21 requests contain at least one NONPHYSICAL point in the source record (673 of 945 points; the 50 kV/s falls to 1.2 V and 0.4 V hold no physical point at all), so whole-request re-runs cover all 673 target points plus the 272 source-physical points, which ride along as controls.  Per-request point sets, stimulus, windows, tmax and timeout_s are unchanged.
tightened_rerun.physicality_bounds: UNCHANGED from grading.physicality.  Declared decision (2026-10-11, before the run): a bounded, junction-clamp-scale undershoot (< 0.5 V past the declared window with positive supply current; 69 source points) STAYS NONPHYSICAL under the existing rule.  A separate flagged class would need its own declared decision and checker change (follow-up work), deliberately not taken here so this record stays a tolerance-only comparison.  The source record's bound is not loosened.
tightened_rerun.cost_rule: pilot representative requests on the batch fleet first, measure per-corner runtime against the source record, and project every remaining request against the enforced per-job limit (tightened_rerun.job_limit_s) before submitting it; split or defer only with the projection recorded
tightened_rerun.job_limit_note: OBSERVED enforced limit, set 2026-10-12: the runner executed both reltol2e-4 pilot jobs under `timeout 3600s` (klt stderr; jobs klt-sim-c3ba332c37d3 and klt-sim-fd2409da90fb, elapsed 3605/3604 s) and ignored the requests' declared options.timeout_s=7200.  3600 s is the conservative, observed ceiling; the 7200 s request declaration is kept unchanged in build_request because changing it is a runner-side question (2AMLogic/klayout-tools).
tightened_rerun.pilot_rationale: control is the cheapest default-deck job (450 s, 18 targets + 27 controls) and cube_v1.2_h0.0001_f50000_r10000 is a mid-cost (1402 s) request from the 50 kV/s-to-1.2 V class that held no physical point; both are part of the rerun set, so the pilot jobs are kept as rerun evidence, not discarded.  The projection applies the LARGEST observed tightened/default ratio (whole-job elapsed or summed per-corner runtime) to every request's default-deck elapsed time; a request projected over job_limit_s is not submitted whole until a split is declared.  Re-piloted under reltol2e-4-klu after variant_decision (2026-10-12): the reltol2e-4 SPARSE pilots timed out, so the new variant must re-earn its projection from its own pilot jobs; those timed-out SPARSE jobs stay in record 20261011-214916-183a3fc.
tightened_rerun.control_policy: changed control verdicts (source-physical point changing verdict under the tightened deck, either direction) are evidence: both outcomes are retained in the per-point comparison, never discarded, and control agreement is NOT a precondition for publishing this record

fleet.backend: batch (Spot fleet) via klt sim --backend batch, one request per dip point = 45 PVT corners; no local grid execution.  A single local corner probe (--backend local) is permitted for netlist validation only.
fleet.ngspice_note: The fleet runner ignores options.ngspice_init, so ng_nomodcheck is carried in the netlist body as in supply-ramp-top.
